autobiographical_memories.title: The Jack Webb meeting at Universal and the walk back to Burbank
autobiographical_memories.summary: Robert recalls attending a Friday-night meeting at Universal while homeless in Los Angeles, briefly feeling he belonged inside the studio, then walking toward Burbank and sleeping beside a freeway.
anchors: Robert says he was homeless in Los Angeles and fighting to clear his name during repeated court dates; no exact date was supplied.

He attended a Friday-night Alcoholics Anonymous meeting called the Jack Webb meeting to gain legitimate access to Universal Studios because he loved movies and television. He said alcohol was not why he went and did not describe himself as an alcoholic.
He now believes the entrance was Gate 5 on Lankershim Boulevard. Saying Jack Webb to the guard led to an ordinary paper pass and entry.
He remembers Building 2250, the Jack Webb Building, and a large framed picture of Jack Webb. Dragnet's just the facts resonated with his efforts to get the facts of his case considered.
He attended and listened, then left through the same gate and walked through Toluca Lake at night toward Burbank, passing lit stores and restaurants.
Near Bob Hope Drive and a freeway ramp he went between bushes and a brick wall, climbed toward the freeway, and slept beside a large bush with traffic audible all night.
The memory contrasts moments inside Hollywood with still needing somewhere safe to sleep. His account ends: The next morning the traffic was still there. So was I.
uncertainties: Exact Friday, calendar date and year are unknown.
Gate 5 is Robert's present belief, not a confirmed gate identification.
Building number, route and events are his reported recollection; no independent verification was performed.
Attendance does not establish alcohol dependence, a diagnosis, court outcome, or meeting with Jack Webb himself.

autobiographical_memories.title: The Ghostbusters car and the Superman figure left behind
autobiographical_memories.summary: On the move from Mobile to Indianapolis, Robert chose a large Ghostbusters car while hoping to recover the Superman figure he had left behind. Superman represented hope during a painful childhood. His later reflections include both hurt and a wish to speak with David again.
anchors: Robert left Mobile, Alabama, for Indianapolis and was upset that his Superman action figure had been left behind.
At a store on the journey he was allowed to choose a toy and picked a large Ghostbusters car that could hold action figures.
He thinks part of him imagined eventually recovering Superman and putting him in that car. He says he never saw the Superman figure again.
He describes Superman as a source of hope and the figure as close to a friend during abuse by William; keep the painful history high-level unless Robert invites detail.
David McMurrer was his stepfather then and later adopted him. Brian is his younger half-brother and Christina his older sister. Robert recalls feeling treated less fairly than them.
Robert reflects that experiences shaped him without erasing their painful parts. His retrospective meaning should not be turned into a claim that abuse was justified or beneficial.
David has died, according to Robert's post. Robert wishes he could sit down with him as the person he is today, ask unanswered questions, and say things he did not get to say.
